values:
This mandatory audit collects data on community bed numbers, length of stay, purposes, and how they are commissioned.

As bed capacity can be changeable, the audit asked for a ‘snapshot’ of bed usage and provision as close as possible to midnight on Wednesday 4 March 2026.

The scope of this data collection includes all NHS, jointly commissioned and Better Care Fund (BCF) funded beds used for intermediate care purposes.

Purpose of the service provided at the chosen snapshot of time
Indication of names likely to be used locally
Community rehab, reablement and recovery beds
1.Short-term services for rehabilitation, recovery and/or reablement post-hospital treatment
Pathway 2 (P2); Intermediate Care; Step down; Rehab:  non-weight-bearing; short-term services/ placement (STS / STP); frailty

Short-term rehabilitation and/or reablement services provided in a bedded setting to support recovery and regain independence after an episode of hospital treatment. Service is open to anyone aged 18+ who could benefit from an appropriate level of rehab/ reablement which cannot be provided in their usual place of residence and does not need specialised services.
2.Short-term services for rehabilitation, recovery and/or reablement post-hospital treatment for stroke or neuro intermediate care
Stroke rehabilitation beds, Neuro rehabilitation beds
Short-term rehabilitation and/or reablement aligned to stroke/neuro clinical pathways to regain independence but not provided through specialised commissioning arrangements.
3.Short-term services for rehabilitation, recovery and/or reablement post-hospital treatment for bariatrics intermediate care
Short-term rehabilitation and/or reablement aligned to bariatrics clinical pathways to regain independence but not provided through specialised commissioning arrangements.
4.Short-term services for rehabilitation, recovery and/or reablement post-hospital treatment for amputee rehabilitation
Short-term rehabilitation and/or reablement aligned to amputee clinical pathways to regain independence but not provided through specialised commissioning arrangements.
5.Short-term services for rehabilitation, recovery and/or reablement post-hospital treatment for other more complex or specialist requirements
Short-term rehabilitation and/or reablement aligned to other specific clinical pathways to regain independence but not provided through specialised commissioning arrangements.
6.Short-term services for rehabilitation, recovery and/or reablement post-hospital treatment for people with confusion/ delirium/ dementia
Older person’s mental health (EMI, OPMH+), confusion, dementia and delirium; high dependency
Short-term bedded services to enable older people with more complex mental health needs to access short-term rehabilitation, reablement and recovery services.
Step up beds; admission avoidance; prevention

Short-term rehabilitation and/or reablement services provided in a bedded setting directly accessed by primary care and community nursing, amongst other services, to prevent escalation of condition. Rapid service delivery that aims to prevent further deconditioning.
Other community bed purposes in scope
D2A; Transition; waiting beds; CHC; low level assistance: Pathway 3 D2A

Temporary bedded services for extremely frail people who have been clinically assessed as requiring a permanent P3 placement in a care/nursing home but are waiting for a permanent bed to become available or for aspects such as funding to be finalised.
9.Period of recovery and prevention of homelessness
Support for people leaving hospital to avoid homelessness. Recovery services might be focused on life skills and emotional support as well as or instead of rehabilitation, depending on the individual
